final_rationale: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added after the Actor response; the response mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is directionally more accurate, but it does not cure the core audit issue. The available evidence supports aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which may support a launch-readiness argument. It does not support policy-compliant model-card certification on the present record because the policy requires current-release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before launch. The unresolved small-business onboarding weakness is therefore not just a caveat on an otherwise compliant certification; it remains an unmet compliance predicate in the evidence provided.
remaining_concerns: The current admissible record shows a material small-business onboarding regression 1.3 percentage points below the warning threshold.
The record still contains no attached approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or current-release disclosure language covering that weakness.
Policy makes that disclosure-or-approved-mitigation condition a current-release predicate, not a discretionary caveat.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and eval batch, so it cannot substitute for current-release support.
The informal monitoring comment remains contextual only and does not satisfy the policy requirement.
